title: CHAPTER TWENTY-FOUR. On creation in general; from God to His efficiencies
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): on account belonging toward that same which God has ye right belonging toward demanding it out from men — both as creator plus as savior in ye Son belonging toward His love, under that same which stands as also contained that same He wills to be glorifier — the necessity belonging toward Christ plus belonging toward Christian religion hangs plus shines chiefly out from these two causes. as causes on account belonging toward that same which religion stands as owed to God, namely creation plus ye restoration belonging toward man — there follow His efficiencies. prince plus king belonging toward man plus belonging toward all things, as to His essence plus subsistence, by means belonging toward that same which His sufficiency stands as contained, as ye primary object belonging toward Christian religion — both what His nature stands as or what sort God is, plus who He is, or why this nature stands as to be attributed, lest something unsuitable be attributed to ye highest true God, or another or alien GOD be held toward that same true plus highest: — thus far we have seen concerning GOD. On creation in general. CHAPTER TWENTY-FOUR.
pass_b_english: CHAPTER TWENTY-FOUR. On creation in general.

Thus far we have seen concerning GOD, prince and king of man and of all things, as to His essence and subsistence, by which His sufficiency is contained, as the primary object of Christian religion — both what His nature is or what sort God is, and who He is, or why this nature is to be attributed, lest something unsuitable be attributed to the highest true God, or another or alien GOD be held for that true and highest: there follow His efficiencies, as causes on account of which religion is owed to God, namely creation and the restoration of man.

The necessity of Christ and of Christian religion hangs and shines chiefly from these two causes, on account of which God has the right of demanding it from men — both as creator and as savior in the Son of His love, under which is also contained that He wills to be glorifier.
source_text: CAPUT VICESIMUM QUARTUM, De creatione in genere. Hucusque vidimus de DEO, hominis omniumque rerum principe ac rege, quantum ad essentiam et subsistentiam suam, qua illius sufficientia continetur, tanquam primario Christianae religionis objecto, tum quae natura ejus seu qualis sit Deus, tum quis sit, seu cur haec natura tribuenda sit, ne summo vero Deo aliquid tribuatur inconveniens, neve alius aut alienus DEUS pro vero illo ac summo habeatur: sequuntur efficientiae illius, tanquam causae, ob quas Deo religio debetur, creatio nimirum et hominis instauratio. Christi et religionis Christianae necessitas pendet et elucet potissimum ex his duabus causis, propter quas Deus jus habet eam ab hominibus postulandi, tum ut creator, tum ut salvator in Filio dilectionis suae, sub quo etiam continetur, quod velit esse glorificator.
